top_story.headline: Rep. Michael T. McCaul filed his 2025 annual disclosure 62 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: The House Clerk record shows a second McCaul filing, a periodic transaction report, posted the same day.
paragraphs: Deadline Watch flags Rep. Michael T. McCaul (R-TX-10) for filing his calendar-year 2025 annual financial disclosure on October 14, 2026, which is 62 days after his final extension date. That is a late disclosure.

The same day, a periodic transaction report under McCaul's name was posted. The text could not be parsed into trade lines because it is a scanned image or unusual layout, so nothing is reported here about its contents.

The rest of the window was quiet. There were no new Office of Government Ethics filings and no new FARA filings, and no new presidential or vice-presidential 278-Ts. Three lobbying reports name the President or Vice President as an entity lobbied (see the first section).

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: No FARA contacts to report; three lobbying reports name the President or Vice President
paragraphs: The FARA scan found no new filings naming the President, Vice President or a cabinet member. Three Lobbying Disclosure Act third-quarter reports list the White House as an entity lobbied. None of them describes a specific meeting, call or text.

items: Anchor & Arrow LLC for client American Phalanx: lists the Office of the Vice President among the entities lobbied. Issues: defense acquisition policy reform, defense innovation, American technology leadership initiatives and maritime domain awareness. Filing.

Catholic Health Association of the United States (self-filed): lists the President among the entities lobbied. Issues include H.R. 1144, the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention Protection and Reauthorization Act of 2025, and H.R. 529, the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act. Filing.

Shield AI (self-filed): lists the Vice President among the entities lobbied. Issues: the National Defense Authorization Act, defense appropriations, autonomy and artificial intelligence, FAA regulations and foreign military sales. Filing.

sections.headline: No new OGE ethics filings this window
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics filing system had no new divestitures, ethics agreements, or other flagged filings in the period of October 13–17.

sections.headline: Five House filings, including two periodic transaction reports with parsed trades
paragraphs: Five House filings and no Senate filings came in over the window. Two periodic transaction reports have parsed trades: one from Rep. Scott H. Peters (bond-heavy) and one from Rep. David J. Taylor (small stock trades). Neither carries a late flag. Rep. Michael T. McCaul filed a periodic transaction report with no parsed trades.

items: Rep. Scott H. Peters (CA50), periodic transaction report filed October 15: four spouse-owned transactions, three purchases and one sale, all government-securities or bond assets. They are two California state general obligation bond purchases on September 3 ($250,001-$500,000 and $100,001-$250,000), a Charlotte-Mecklenburg hospital bond purchase on September 25 ($250,001-$500,000) and a U.S. Treasury bill sale on September 24 ($250,001-$500,000). None is marked late. Filing.

Rep. David J. Taylor (OH02), periodic transaction report filed October 15: four stock trades, all $1,001-$15,000. He bought AT&T Inc., Fifth Third Bancorp and RPM International Inc. on October 9, and sold Procter & Gamble Company on October 12. None is marked late. Filing.
Rep. Michael T. McCaul (TX10), periodic transaction report filed October 14: a scanned or unreadable filing with no trade lines parsed. Filing.

sections.headline: 25 new registrations and a heavy third-quarter reporting wave, led by defense, energy and former-staff lobbyists
paragraphs: The listing covers 750 filings posted since October 15; the fetch stopped after 30 pages, so more exist. By type: 579 third-quarter reports, 78 third-quarter no-activity reports, 25 registrations, 21 no-activity terminations, 20 third-quarter terminations, 13 first-quarter amendments, 7 third-quarter amendments, and a handful of second-quarter and other filings.

Skyline Capitol LLC, whose lobbyists include former Rep. Chris Stewart (2013-2023), ended or reported on a long list of clients. The table covers every new registration and every termination that reported activity. Roughly 20 no-activity terminations are left out as routine. Of the 681 activity reports, the table carries only a few of the 330 flagged as having a signal; the rest are counted, not described.
